I’m a lifelong critical thinker, mother, and South Carolina resident who believes ideas should be challenged, not protected from scrutiny.

I’m the mom of two incredible kids, including my son Peyton, who died from a rare and aggressive brain cancer. Being a childhood cancer mom permanently reshaped how I see healthcare, policy, power, and who pays the price when systems fail. Grief stripped away my tolerance for performative politics and forced me to care deeply about what actually works.

My values are rooted in logic, compassion, and accountability. I believe policies should be evidence-based, ethically defensible, and centered on real human outcomes, not ideology, party loyalty, or religious doctrine. I’m skeptical by nature, allergic to slogans, and deeply uninterested in outrage-for-profit discourse.

I’ve lived across socioeconomic classes, navigated broken healthcare systems firsthand, and spent years studying economics, politics, and belief systems through both lived experience and formal learning. My views are not static. They evolve when confronted with better data or stronger arguments.

I’m here to engage in thoughtful, good-faith discussion, push back where necessary, and learn where possible. I value respectful disagreement and believe democracy only works when people are willing to think out loud, change their minds, and hold power to account.

If you’re here for nuance, curiosity, and honest conversation, we’ll get along just fine.
